ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, composed of small squares with a side length of 1, points A, B, and C are all located at the intersections of the grid lines. Circle $O$ with AB as its diameter passes through point C. If point D is on circle $O$, then what is the value of $\tan \angle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $AC$ and $BC$, \\
since $AB$ is the diameter of the circle $O$, \\
it follows that $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, \\
since $\angle ABC = \angle ADC$, \\
it follows that $\tan\angle ADC = \tan\angle ABC = \frac{AC}{BC} = \boxed{\frac{4}{3}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a dashed grid made up of small squares with side length 1. A, B, C, and D are all on the same circle, and the center of the circle is labeled O; segment AB is the diameter of the circle. A is at the upper left, C is at the upper right, B is at the lower right, and D is at the lower left. After connecting AC and BC, it can be counted from the grid that AC is horizontal 4 units, and BC is vertical 3 units. Reasoning: Because AB is the diameter of circle O, and C is on the circle, by the theorem of the inscribed angle subtended by a diameter, ∠ACB = 90°. Therefore triangle ABC is a right triangle. ∠ADC and ∠ABC are both inscribed angles, and both subtend the same chord AC, so ∠ADC = ∠ABC. Thus tan∠ADC = tan∠ABC. In right triangle ABC, for angle ABC, the opposite side is AC and the adjacent side is BC, so tan∠ABC = AC/BC = 4/3. Therefore tan∠ADC = 4/3.
